## The first table

Day 1 uses 72 mice and three protein signals: BDNF, pCREB and NR1. Treatment groups contain different animals, and both groups include the two genotypes and learning protocols.

One row is one mouse, using assay record 1 from that mouse. The original study measured each sample repeatedly; those repeated readings are not extra mice.

| Column in study.csv | Meaning |
|---|---|
| sample_id | Animal identifier |
| group | Saline or Memantine |
| BDNF | BDNF assay signal (relative units) |
| pCREB | pCREB assay signal (relative units) |
| NR1 | NR1/GluN1 assay signal (relative units) |
| genotype | Control or Ts65Dn |
| learning | C/S or S/C |
| source_record | Original assay record retained |

The column names identify the biological measurements;
always give the full measurement and units in a plot caption or report. CSVs are UTF-8,
comma-separated, with a header. `NA` denotes missing. Raw files are not changed by the
interactive controls or by the made-up outlier/missingness exercises.

## Mouse data: preparation and limits

Higuera, Gardiner and Cios (2015), UCI Mice Protein Expression, DOI 10.24432/C50S3Z.
Dataset licence: **CC BY 4.0**, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/.
The preparation described here is our teaching adaptation; the raw values are preserved.

The workbook has 1,080 assay rows for 72 mice, with 77 protein/modification signals.
The study describes three replicates of a five-point dilution series per mouse.
**We consistently retain the record whose MouseID ends in `_1`.** This rule is independent
of the measured result. We do not average across dilution levels or pretend to reconstruct
the original mixed-effects analysis. This is a deliberately reduced assay-level teaching
comparison, with one selected signal per animal; it sacrifices information and precision.
The source does not establish record 1 as an optimal abundance estimate. Do not label these
values as absolute concentrations or as fold changes in cognitive ability.

`study.csv` contains all 72 mice at that selected record:

| Column | Meaning / unit |
|---|---|
| sample_id | Original mouse identifier without the assay suffix; nominal ID |
| genotype | Control or Ts65Dn (trisomic mouse model); nominal |
| group | Saline or Memantine; nominal |
| learning | C/S = context then shock; S/C = shock then context; nominal protocol |
| BDNF | Source BDNF_N signal, relative assay units |
| pCREB | Source pCREB_N signal, relative assay units |
| NR1 | Source NR1_N signal, relative assay units |
| source_record | Complete original MouseID, e.g. 309_1 |

The `_N` source suffix indicates nuclear fraction. Values are the provided continuous assay
signals, without rescaling or rounding. Blank source cells become `NA`; no imputation,
outlier removal or selection by significance is performed. Missingness must be handled
for each analysis. Correlations between assay signals can also reflect shared measurement
procedures; they do not establish direct molecular regulation.

`study.csv` uses `group` to name the treatment. It retains genotype, learning protocol and source record. All three selected signals are observed in all 72 mice.

We use **all 72 mice: 34 Saline and 38 Memantine**, with all three protein measurements available at the selected record. **Treatments are unpaired:** each mouse received one treatment; no mouse appears in both groups. The three proteins are measured in the same mouse, which lets us study their association. Both treatment groups contain different genotypes and learning protocols. Pooled comparisons describe this mixed cohort; they do not isolate a drug effect or demonstrate improved memory.

Animal independence remains a design assumption; the table does not document all possible cage or litter dependence.

## Reproducibility

The raw workbook, its SHA-256 checksum and exact download URL are preserved in `instructor/source/mouse/`
in the branch checkout (excluded from the small student ZIP). `scripts/validate_data.py` reconciles selected mouse measurements and the MMSE first visits with the archived sources. Original preparation scripts are archived with notes on their original paths. No outcomes were changed to manufacture a result.

[Dataset](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/342/mice+protein+expression) · [Study](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0129126)

## Archived assay records

`replicates.csv` preserves all 1,080 source records for provenance, including BDNF, pCREB and NR1. Workshop exercises use the 72-row animal table throughout. The raw record index is not a time variable.

# Larger dataset: `mmse_baseline.csv`

One first visit for each of **136 participants**, with 72 source-labelled Nondemented and 64 Demented. The measurements come from the previous course's `alzheimer_data.csv`; all retained values and their numerical precision are preserved. Eight SES values are missing (`NA`); there are no missing MMSE values in this first-visit subset. `NA` is not zero.

The previous file contained 336 visits with participant and visit columns removed. We matched its row references and every retained variable to the [official OASIS-2 demographics workbook](https://sites.wustl.edu/oasisbrains/files/2024/03/oasis_longitudinal_demographics-8d83e569fa2e2d30.xlsx), allowing only the existing rounding of imaging values. This restored identifiers and made selection of `Visit == 1` possible. No participant was selected on the basis of their MMSE value or a test result.

The original OASIS-2 workbook contains 373 visits from 150 participants. The source's Converted group was already excluded from the previous course file. This teaching version keeps that exclusion: its group labels describe longitudinal classification, not an independently reconstructed baseline diagnosis. Selection based on longitudinal group membership limits generalisation. The core analysis is cross-sectional and cannot measure individual change over time. See the [OASIS-2 study description](https://sites.wustl.edu/oasisbrains/home/oasis-2/).

| Column | Definition and unit | Measurement type |
|---|---|---|
| `Source_row` | Row number in the original demographic table, excluding the header | Provenance identifier |
| `Subject_ID` | Original participant identifier | Identifier; unique in this file |
| `Visit` | Visit number; all values are 1 | Visit index |
| `Group` | Source longitudinal classification, Nondemented or Demented | Nominal |
| `M.F` | Source-recorded M/F category | Nominal |
| `Age` | Age at the visit in years | Numeric, recorded in whole years |
| `EDUC` | Years of education | Numeric, recorded in whole years |
| `SES` | Hollingshead categories, 1 highest status to 5 lowest | Ordinal; equal gaps are not assumed |
| `MMSE` | Cognitive assessment score, 0–30 | Discrete, bounded score |
| `CDR` | Clinical Dementia Rating: 0 none, 0.5 very mild, 1 mild, 2 moderate | Ordinal; not an equal-interval scale |
| `eTIV` | Estimated total intracranial volume, cm³ | Numeric |
| `nWBV` | Normalised whole-brain volume: tissue fraction within the atlas-masked image; 0.70 corresponds to 70% | Numeric fraction, not a raw volume in cm³ |
| `ASF` | Atlas scaling factor used to map the native image to the atlas | Numeric, unitless |

Definitions follow the measures in [Marcus et al. (2010), OASIS longitudinal MRI data, Table 4](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2895005/). The CSV stores nWBV as a fraction, although the paper describes the corresponding percentage. eTIV and ASF are related to head size and image scaling; neither should be treated as an independent measure of cognitive performance.

MMSE and the clinical grouping are related assessments. A group difference in MMSE does not independently validate a diagnostic test. These participants were not randomly assigned to groups, so age, education, selection, and other factors may affect comparisons.


The OASIS and legacy source tables are preserved in `instructor/source/mmse/`. Day 2 uses only mmse_baseline.csv. No measurements have been changed for this combined course.
